core_obligations: Record that O_{X,x} is a Noetherian local domain of dimension one because X is a curve (proof lines 9375-9376).
Show that (4) and (5) are equivalent by definition and equivalent to the maximal ideal I_x = m_x being generated by one element, via the effective Cartier criterion (proof lines 9377-9379).
Conclude the equivalence of (1), (2), (3), (4) and (5) from the algebra characterization of discrete valuation rings (proof lines 9380-9381).

Prove the additional equivalence with smoothness at x: in the perfect case via the dense smooth open lemma, and when kappa(x)/k is separable via the separable-smoothness algebra lemma (proof lines 9382-9384).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain.
Translate the divisor conditions into principality of the maximal ideal.
Apply the discrete valuation ring characterization.
Handle the smoothness equivalence in the perfect and separable cases.
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the equivalence of five conditions on a closed point x of a curve over a field - regularity, normality, discrete valuation ring, invertibility of the ideal sheaf of x, and x being an effective Cartier divisor - and adds smoothness of X over k at x under a perfectness or separability hypothesis. The proof uses that the local ring at a closed point of a curve is a Noetherian local domain of dimension one, identifies conditions (4) and (5) with the maximal ideal being principal via the effective Cartier criterion, and applies the algebra characterization of discrete valuation rings to conclude the equivalence of (1) to (5) (proof lines 9375-9381). The smoothness statement is deduced from the dense smooth open lemma in the perfect case and from the separable-smoothness algebra lemma when the residue field is separable (proof lines 9382-9384). H2: the reduction to the principal-maximal-ideal criterion and the two smoothness routes are the substance.
